newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-FRANCE-ENGLAND BATTLE AT DEAUVILLE.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-FRANCE-ENGLAND BATTLE AT DEAUVILLE.

text.p: The group one Prix
Maurice de Gheest is set to be a straight shoot out between
France and Britain on Sunday.
Heading the French hopes are Titus Livius, a good second in
the group two King's Stand Stakes at Royal Ascot, and Nombre
Premier, a good third in the group three Prix de Ris-Orangis
last month.
The home challenge also includes useful types such as
Winning Smile, Occupandiste and Wardara, although they may be a
few pounds below the required standard.
The cross-channel challenge is spearheaded by the remarkable
six-year-old Monaassib, who still seems to be improving judged
on his game Ris-Orangis success. The Ed Dunlop charge has been
beaten only once in six starts this term, but, like Nombre
Premier, he will need the ground to be good or better.
It was riding soft on Thursday, but it is expected to dry
out.
The British challenge also includes useful customers such as
Godolphin's Kahal and Richard Hannon's Deadly Dudley.
Kahal was a good second to Among Men in the group three
Jersey Stakes while the well regarded Deadly Dudley has not been
out since taking the Criterium des Deux Ans, a group two race,
at Evry last November.
